`test-suggest.yml` has Claude review each function together with its
existing tests. It writes new `testthat` tests where they add value, fixes
or removes existing tests that no longer fit, **runs every new or changed
test**, and proposes only what passes as a [suggestion PR](suggestions.qmd).

## What it does

- **Every function is reviewed**, whether it already has tests or not —
  the changed ones in a PR, and in a [sweep](#sweep-scope) the recently
  changed ones plus a rotating share of the rest.
- **New tests only where they add value.** Claude names the value of each
  test — an uncovered code path, error handling, an edge case, or a likely
  regression — and tests without such a reason are dropped, as are copies
  of existing tests. See [what gets proposed](suggestions.qmd#what-gets-proposed).
  At most 10 new tests per function.
- **Existing tests are reviewed too** — see [below](#existing-tests).
- **Every test is run** with your package loaded from source before it is
  proposed.
- **No setup needed.** A package without `testthat` gets it set up in the
  same suggestion PR: `tests/testthat.R`, `testthat` in `Suggests`, and
  `Config/testthat/edition: 3` (only when the test runner is created; an
  existing suite keeps its edition).

One test file per function is assumed: `tests/testthat/test-<function>.R`.

The review uses a stronger Claude model than the
[roxygen suggestions](roxygen-suggest.qmd), with extended thinking:
deciding which tests add value, and why an existing test fails, needs more
careful reasoning than documentation.

## What Claude gets

Besides the function and its test file:

- **The results of the existing tests**, run before anything is changed.
- **The history**: when the function and its test file last changed, and
  in a PR whether the function changed without its test — with the diff.
- **Your test support files** (`tests/testthat/setup*.R`, `helper*.R`)
  verbatim, so the tests use your own objects and helper functions.
- **The structure of the test data** those files create: for each table
  its rows, columns, types and missing values, and for factors the counts
  per level. The level counts are the only data values sent to Claude.

## Test quality

Claude is asked to write tests that

- assert **concrete values** from the known test data (counts, levels,
  dimensions), not just a class;
- always assert something — no `if (...) expect_...`;
- never swallow errors or warnings with `try()` / `tryCatch()`, but check
  them with `expect_error()` / `expect_warning()`;
- test each error branch once;
- describe exactly what they check.

## Existing tests {#existing-tests}

Claude also decides on existing tests, and states a reason for each:

| Action | Reason | When |
|---|---|---|
| Update | `contract_changed` | The function was changed on purpose and the test still expects the old behaviour |
| Delete | `duplicate`, `behavior_removed`, `trivial` | The test repeats another, tests something the function no longer does, or asserts nothing meaningful |
| Report | `possible_code_bug` | The test fails, and the code rather than the test looks wrong |

Safeguards apply before anything is changed:

- **Only a failing test is updated.** A passing test is never rewritten.
- **A test is never adapted to output that may be wrong.** If the code may
  be at fault, the test stays and is reported instead.
- **An update must pass a real run**; otherwise the original test is kept
  and the attempt is reported.

## The report

The link comment on your PR and the suggestion PR's description start with
a one-line summary, e.g. "7 new tests · 1 existing test updated". The
description then lists, grouped per test file in collapsible sections:

- **Changes to existing tests**, each with its reason;
- **Existing tests to look at** — reported tests and failing tests left
  unchanged;
- in a sweep, **generated tests that failed** (see below).

Heading sizes and spacing can be adjusted in `config/report-style.yml`
([per repository](suggestions.qmd#adjusting-the-guidance)). Without a
suggestion PR, the report is posted as a comment on your PR, or in a sweep
as one issue.

## Failing tests

A generated test that fails is not proposed. Claude classifies why it
failed, from the actual error output, and the workflow reports it:

| Classification | Meaning | Reported as |
|---|---|---|
| `real_bug` | The test is right and found a defect | An issue |
| `bad_test` | The test itself is wrong | A comment on your PR |
| `env_misconfiguration` | The test setup is broken, e.g. a missing package | A comment on your PR |

In a sweep there is no PR to comment on, so the last two are listed in the
sweep PR's description instead, or in one issue if no test passed at all.

## Sweep scope {#sweep-scope}

A [sweep](suggestions.qmd#sweeps) doesn't review every function every
month. It takes the functions whose file or test file changed within
`sweep-lookback-days` (default 35), plus a rotating share of the rest, so
that each function comes up at least once every `sweep-rotation-months`
(default 6). Set `sweep-rotation-months: 0` to review all functions in
every sweep.

## DataSHIELD client packages

Client-side functions need a DataSHIELD server. With `datashield: true` and
`datashield-type: client`, tests run against
[DSLite](https://github.com/datashield/DSLite), an in-process server:

- An **existing DSLite setup** in any `tests/testthat/setup*.R` or
  `helper*.R` is reused, with your own connection names, symbols and
  helpers.
- Otherwise one is **created** with one of DSLite's bundled datasets, in
  `tests/testthat/setup.R` — or in `setup-dslite.R` if a `setup.R`
  without DSLite already exists, which is never touched.

::: {.callout-important}
DSLite takes the server functions from the **installed server packages**.
List them (e.g. `dsBase`), together with `DSLite` and `testthat`, in your
`DESCRIPTION` — for example under `Suggests` — so the workflow installs
them. Otherwise every test fails as `env_misconfiguration`.
:::
